learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of creating your first bootstrap web page and when it is appropriate.
Apply standard html document structure using the documented Bootstrap 5.3 pattern.
Check adding bootstrap styles and identify one likely failure mode.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will study creating your first bootstrap web page and connect it to a small implementation or review task. The included subtopics preserve the attached Bootstrap curriculum outline.
content.why_it_matters: Creating Your First Bootstrap Web Page helps you decide how to introduce Bootstrap without confusing presentation styles with application behavior. Start from semantic HTML, add the framework deliberately, and verify the result in a browser.

content_blocks.run_instructions: Save the snippet as index.html and open it in a modern browser with internet access to the pinned Bootstrap 5.3.8 CDN. It is a visual preview, not a server-side application.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the original example, undo one change at a time, and repeat the same browser/build check. Do not keep temporary debugging rules in the final implementation.

content_blocks.title: Professional habit
content_blocks.text: Use the pinned Bootstrap 5.3.x baseline, follow the official component documentation, and verify semantic HTML, responsive behavior, and keyboard access before reusing the pattern.

content.task: Create a small page that demonstrates creating your first bootstrap web page and write one sentence explaining why you chose a CDN or package-manager setup.
task_acceptance_criteria: Explain the purpose and appropriate use of creating your first bootstrap web page.
Use the documented class, component, API, or workflow correctly.
Record a responsive, accessibility, or build verification relevant to this example.
hints: Start with the smallest source example in this lesson.
Change one class, attribute, or configuration item at a time.
Compare expected behavior with the result; consult the linked official page if the version-specific behavior differs.
content.expected_output: A working or reviewed example of creating your first bootstrap web page, with a short explanation and recorded verification steps.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating creating your first bootstrap web page as a visual-only change.
common_mistakes.why: A class or style does not automatically add semantic meaning, application logic, or secure server behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Use the appropriate HTML semantics and verify the actual interaction.

common_mistakes.problem: Checking only the default viewport or happy path.
common_mistakes.why: Responsive changes and interaction states can reveal issues that are not visible in a single screenshot.
common_mistakes.fix: Repeat the task at a narrow and a wide viewport and include keyboard/error state checks where relevant.
